svg.title: mike two-phase capture write, animated
svg.desc: Animated sequence diagram. The proxy keeps the inbound bytes, attempts a Phase-1 stub row before forwarding, writes canonical stream blocks and tool-use rows as the SSE stream arrives, writes a Phase-2 terminal snapshot at message_stop, creates agent instances on primary turns, and a NOTIFY updates the web UI.
svg.text: Two capture phases, with incremental writes between them

g.text: A captured request needs a canonical session-id header; without one it is forwarded with no row at all.
engine::accept keeps the untouched inbound body before any stage runs.
Phase 1: stub insert, before the upstream call
With persistence, insert_stub_and_mint_id establishes the durable RequestId; failed writes can leave gaps.
The parser task updates the in-memory InterceptedRequest as events arrive.
On the plain path Claude Code gets each chunk as it arrives.
Canonical responses.stream_blocks writes land between the phases; they reference the durable request.
Tool calls, as each one finishes
write_tool_use_row fires per ToolUseEnd event, before the terminal snapshot.
Non-streaming responses reach the same point through complete_non_streaming.
The terminal snapshot persists response and diagnostics, plus lifecycle/projection updates; not one SQL write.
Creates agent_instances rows and back-fills sub-agent requests. Soft-fails; never breaks the hot path.
NOTIFY proxy.row_changed → db_listener → ProxyEvent::RowChanged → every /api/ws subscriber.
